parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A diffraction grating has 5200 lines per centimetre. Light contains wavelengths 656.478 nm and 656.296 nm. Calculate the larger of their second-order diffraction angles for normal incidence.

answer.text: The line density is 5.20×10⁵ m⁻¹, so d=1/(5.20×10⁵)=1.923×10⁻⁶ m. The larger wavelength gives the larger angle. Using d sinθ=nλ with n=2 gives θ=sin⁻¹(2×656.478×10⁻⁹/d)=43.06°, about 43.1°.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: White light with wavelengths from 400 nm to 700 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating with 400 lines per millimetre. (a) Find the angular width of the second-order spectrum on one side of the central maximum. (b) Find the largest order that can contain the entire wavelength range.

answer.text: (a) d=1/(4.00×10⁵)=2.50×10⁻⁶ m. In order n=2, θ400=sin⁻¹(2×400×10⁻⁹/d)=18.66° and θ700=34.06°. The width is their difference, 15.39°, about 15.4°. (b) Every wavelength must satisfy nλ≤d. The longest wavelength is limiting, so n≤2500/700=3.57. The largest complete order is 3.

evidence.review: Derived independently from the question and checked against the first-assessment2025 IB Physics guide; handwritten annotations are not answer evidence.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Light falls normally on a diffraction grating. For its maxima, nλ = d sin θ. Which identification is incorrect?

A. d is the distance from grating to screen
B. λ is the wavelength
C. n is the order of the maximum
D. θ is the angle of the maximum from the forward direction

answer.text: A. d is the separation of adjacent grating slits, not the distance to the screen.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Light is incident normally on a diffraction grating with 300 lines per mm. A graph of order n against sin θ has gradient G. Which expression gives the wavelength in metres?

A. 3 × 10⁵G
B. 3.3 × 10⁻⁶G
C. (3.3 × 10⁻⁶)/G
D. 300/G

answer.text: C. nλ = d sin θ means n = (d/λ) sin θ, so G = d/λ. The slit spacing is d = 1/(300 × 1000) = 3.33 × 10⁻⁶ m; therefore λ = d/G.

parts.display_text:
Light of wavelength 567 nm is incident normally on a grating with 400 lines per millimetre. What is the angular separation between the second- and third-order maxima on the same side of the central maximum?

A. 13.1°
B. 13.9°
C. 15.9°
D. 27.0°

answer.text: C. d = 1/(400 × 10³) = 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ m. θ₂ = sin⁻¹(2λ/d) ≈ 26.97° and θ₃ = sin⁻¹(3λ/d) ≈ 42.89°. Their separation is θ₃ − θ₂ ≈ 15.9°.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

answer.text:
Editorial worked explanation, checked against the official mark scheme:

D. From nλ = d sinθ, reducing the wavelength reduces θ and therefore moves the first-order maximum closer to the center.
answer.evidence: Official mark scheme checked on page 6.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Light of frequency 6.7 × 10¹⁴ Hz is incident normally on a diffraction grating with 4.0 × 10⁵ lines m⁻¹. What is the angle between adjacent second- and third-order maxima?

A. 12°
B. 21°
C. 33°
D. 54°

answer.text:
Official key A checked; editorial worked explanation:

A. The wavelength is λ = c/f = 4.48 × 10⁻⁷ m and grating spacing d = 1/(4.0 × 10⁵) = 2.50 × 10⁻⁶ m. From d sinθ = nλ, θ₂ = 21.0° and θ₃ = 32.5°. Their separation is 11.5° ≈ 12°.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
For a grating with N lines per metre, a graph plots sinθ against wavelength λ for nth-order maxima. What is the gradient?

A. Nn
B. N/n
C. n/N
D. 1/(Nn)

answer.text:
Official key A checked; editorial worked explanation:

A. Grating spacing is d=1/N. From d sinθ=nλ, sinθ=nλ/d=nNλ. Therefore the gradient of sinθ against λ is nN.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 May/June 2024 published key A, PDF page 2; explanation is editorial.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The source shows a diffraction grating with adjacent-line spacing d, N total lines, wavelength λ and screen distance L. Which quantities affect the separation of the first-order maxima?

answer.text:
Published key A checked; editorial worked explanation:

A. The first-order angle obeys λ=d sinθ, so changing λ or d changes θ. The screen separation is exactly 2L tanθ in the drawn geometry and is approximately 2Lλ/d at small angle. The total number of illuminated lines N changes sharpness, not the maxima positions. Thus d, λ and L affect separation, while N does not.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9702/12 February/March 2023 published key A, PDF page 3; explanation independently authored and checked.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A single narrow slit is illuminated with monochromatic light. The slit width is increased. What happens to the width and brightness of the central maximum?

A. Width increases; brightness increases
B. Width increases; brightness decreases
C. Width decreases; brightness increases
D. Width decreases; brightness decreases

answer.text:
Published key C checked; editorial worked explanation:

C. The first-minimum angle obeys approximately θ=λ/b, so increasing slit width b narrows the central maximum. A wider slit transmits more light, so the central maximum becomes brighter. It therefore decreases in width and increases in brightness.

evidence.detail: AQA 7408/1 June 2023 published key C, mark-scheme PDF page 26; explanation independently authored and checked.

original-ib26mb2-written-6-e:whole.hint: Convert line density to a slit spacing in metres, then decide which wavelength gives the larger angle at the same order.
notes: Lines per centimetre must be multiplied by 100 to obtain lines per metre. Taking the reciprocal of that density gives the grating spacing.
The order number multiplies wavelength. The normal-incidence grating angle is measured from the straight-through direction, not from the grating surface.

original-ib26mc2-written-5-a-b:whole.hint: Calculate the two boundary angles within the same order. For a complete spectrum, test which wavelength reaches the sine limit first.
notes: Convert line density into reciprocal metres before finding grating spacing. The grating equation uses slit spacing, not the number of lines per unit length.
A maximum order is an integer rounded down. Shorter wavelengths can occur in a higher order even when that order no longer contains the red end of the spectrum.

cross-ca23j1-29:whole.hint: Convert the quoted line density into the separation between adjacent grating lines.
notes: Grating maxima satisfy d sin θ = nλ. If there are N lines per metre, d = 1/N metres.

cross-ca25n12-mcq-29:whole.hint: The relevant path difference is between waves leaving adjacent slits.
notes: If the line density is N per metre, use d = 1/N. Screen distance may help convert a measured spot position into θ, but is not d in the grating equation.
